LESSON: KENYA’S BILL OF RIGHTS - ELDERLY - REFUGEES - MIGRANTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Developments and Governance
Topic 5.3: Kenya’s Bill of Rights - Elderly - Refugees - Migrants
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenya’s Bill of Rights - Elderly - Refugees - Migrants, part of Political Developments and Governance in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we protect the special groups in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explore Kenya’s bill of rights for mutual social well-being,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenya’s Bill of Rights - Elderly - Refugees - Migrants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenya’s Bill of Rights - Elderly - Refugees - Migrants together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: Learners role play situations/scenarios that bring out assertiveness in standing up for individual rights.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners design posters on human rights laws with regard to special groups.

Values:
● Unity: Learners display team sprit as they brainstorm on human rights laws for protection of special groups.

● Patriotism: Learners display a sense of responsibility to the nation as they develop strategies for promoting protection of

special groups in the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Clubs and societies: Learners debate on human rights of special groups.

● Human Rights: Learners brainstorm in groups on human rights laws for protection of special groups.

Link to other learning areas:

● Learners use Religious Education knowledge to develop strategies for promoting protection of special groups in the

community.

● Learners apply English, Kiswahili and Kenya Sign Language knowledge as they debate on human laws for special groups
